title: A failed wall read renders the empty wall, 0/0 locked and 'creation is gated'
body:
## Summary
When the styles store can't be read, the atelier shows the alert and also the zero-styles screen. It then reports 0/0 to the tab rail and says the project gate is shut, so a read failure looks like an empty library.

## Description
lib/useThemes.ts:49-51 handles a read failure with `setThemes([])` + `setError(msg)`. LibraryAtelier then sees `loading=false` (themes !== null) and `rows.length===0`, so it takes the ZERO branch (`LibraryAtelier.tsx:415-416` -> `<EmptyWall/>`, whose Ghost label says 'No styles yet. Start one from the preset rail on the left.'). The onCounts effect at :286-289 only skips `themes === null`, so it reports `{styles:0, locked:0}` and the Styles tab tally (LibraryView.tsx:102-111) shows an amber 0/0 LOCKED. GateChip at :455 reads the same empty array, and its sr-only text says 'No locked style. Project creation is gated.' The code's own comment at :287 says 'an unknown count is not 0', and the FAILURE branch breaks that rule in three places. The Assets side has the same hole in app/library/assets/useShelf.ts:98-101 (owned by the library-assets-audio context, so it isn't in this write_set).

## Flow
- IndexedDB read throws -> useThemes sets themes=[] and error='...'
- Atelier: rose alert + 'The wall is empty' + Ghost telling the user to start a style (wrong remedy: their styles may exist)
- Tab rail: Styles 0/0 LOCKED amber; dossier GateChip: 'Project creation is gated'
- Fix: guard EmptyWall with `!error` (render nothing under the alert when rows are empty and error is set); skip onCounts and GateChip while `error && !rows.length`

## Expected impact
On a failed read the user sees the error and its retry, and nothing claims they have no styles. Today the screen tells them to start over.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a user whose style store fails to read is told they have no styles and should start one
Before: the error+empty render branch draws 3 zero claims (EmptyWall, tab tally 0/0, GateChip 'gated'); stripped LibraryAtelier.tsx has 0 references to `error` in the EmptyWall condition or the onCounts effect
After: 0 zero claims under an error; EmptyWall condition and onCounts effect both reference `error`
Method: probe - source ratchet on stripped LibraryAtelier.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/useThemes.ts:49-51 (setThemes([]) on read failure); app/library/LibraryAtelier.tsx:286-289 (onCounts skips only themes===null), :411-416 (loading ? : !rows.length ? <EmptyWall/>), :455 (<GateChip themes={rows}/>), :532 (Ghost label 'No styles yet. Start one...'); app/library/LibraryView.tsx:102-111 (tally from counts); same pattern app/library/assets/useShelf.ts:98-101 (other context)
verify: tests/golden-path/library-atelier-states.probe.spec.ts: read app/library/LibraryAtelier.tsx, stripComments; (1) slice from the first `loading ?` to `<EmptyWall` and assert it matches /error/; (2) extract the useEffect body that calls `onCounts?.(` and assert it matches /error/. Both red on HEAD, green after. Then npm run typecheck.

title: Full proof sheet silently disables 'render a trial'; its pip row was deleted
body:
## Summary
When a style has 14 approved proofs (PROOF_CAP), the render button is disabled and nothing on screen says why. A comment says a pip row shows this, but that pip row was deleted along with the sheet header.

## Description
parts.tsx:250 passes `disabled={!locked && full}` and Playground.tsx:285 folds it into the button's `disabled`. sheetFull = approvedProofs >= PROOF_CAP (lib/themes.ts:76,218). The comment at parts.tsx:253-257 says 'The full-window sentence became the pip row in the header', but parts.tsx:204-214 records that the header, pip row included, was removed. `PipRow` has 0 consumers under app/library (grep). lockBlocker (lib/themes.ts:249-256) returns null for a fully judged sheet, so SpecEditor shows no text either. The result is a greyed primary CTA with no reason and no next step. The 2026-08-14 Perfect direction 'a-full-proof-sheet-is-not-a-dead-end' (shipped bc09bea) fixed exactly this, and the narration pass undid it. components/ui/signal/README.md already names PipRow as the replacement for this sentence.

## Flow
- Approve the 14th proof
- 'render a trial' goes to opacity-40 and nothing explains it; the lock button stays live
- Fix: in StyleSheet, draw `<PipRow states={approved.map(() => 'filled')} max={PROOF_CAP} label={`${approved.length} of ${PROOF_CAP} reference slots approved`}/>` above the Playground when not locked (import PROOF_CAP from lib/themes). No prose.

## Expected impact
The disabled CTA gets its reason back as a shape, not a sentence. The user can see the window is full, and that rejecting one approved proof or locking are the ways forward.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a full sheet's disabled render button has a visible, accessible reason
Before: PipRow consumers in app/library = 0; full-sheet render branch shows 0 elements explaining the disabled button
After: PipRow rendered in StyleSheet (1 consumer); its aria-label carries the count
Method: probe - source ratchet on stripped parts.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/parts.tsx:200 (full = sheetFull), :250 (disabled={!locked && full}), :204-214 (header removed), :253-257 (comment promising 'the pip row in the header'); app/library/Playground.tsx:285; lib/themes.ts:76 PROOF_CAP=14, :218 sheetFull; grep -rn PipRow app/library -> 0 hits; components/ui/signal/README.md 'PipRow ... Replaces app/library/parts.tsx:265-268 (two sentences to say a reference-image window is full)'; .vault/Perfect/directions/a-full-proof-sheet-is-not-a-dead-end.md (shipped 2026-08-14)
verify: tests/golden-path/library-atelier-states.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(app/library/parts.tsx) must contain `<PipRow` and `PROOF_CAP` (red on HEAD: 0 matches). Also delete or correct the stale comment at parts.tsx:253-257 so it no longer promises a header. npm run typecheck && npm run check:narration.

title: 'style-locked on N proofs' reuses 'locked' for reference conditioning
body:
## Summary
On this surface 'locked' means the permanent ratchet. The playground's reference toggle also uses it, so an unlocked style shows 'style-locked on 3 proofs' right next to a live 'lock this style' button.

## Description
Everywhere else in the atelier and on its tab, 'locked' is the status that freezes a style and opens project creation: STATUS_WORD, SpecEditor.tsx:69 'locked — projects build on this', SpecEditor.tsx:78 'lock this style', the Styles tab tally label 'locked' (LibraryView.tsx:108), GateChip's sr text 'N locked styles'. The Playground checkbox at Playground.tsx:324-332 labels a different thing, 'send my approved proofs as image references', as 'style-locked on N proofs'. It shows whenever approved proofs exist, so on a DRAFT/PROOFING style the user sees 'style-locked' checked while the lock button below says the style isn't locked. On a locked style the same word means two things on one screen. This is one word for two concepts across sibling panes (dossier vs sheet).

## Flow
- Approve 1 proof on a draft style
- Sheet: '[x] style-locked on 1 proof'; dossier: 'lock this style' (enabled) + tab '0/1 LOCKED'
- Fix: relabel to the act it controls, e.g. 'referencing {n} proof(s)' (keep the checkbox, its count and its position; no added prose)

## Expected impact
'locked' means one thing on /library again. Reading the reference toggle can no longer make a user think the irreversible lock already happened.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the word 'locked' names exactly one concept on the Styles tab
Before: rendered strings using 'lock' for a non-ratchet concept = 1 (Playground.tsx:331)
After: 0
Method: probe - source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/Playground.tsx:331 'style-locked on {refs.length} proof(s)'; :163-166 (comment: the toggle exists so the difference can be seen); app/library/SpecEditor.tsx:69,78; app/library/LibraryView.tsx:108 tally label 'locked'; app/library/parts.tsx:473-474 GateChip sr text
verify: tests/golden-path/library-atelier-states.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(app/library/Playground.tsx) must not match /style-locked/ (1 match on HEAD -> 0). Confirm no test asserts the old string: grep -rn 'style-locked' tests uat -> 0.

title: Single-select chips draw 'selected' by colour only — no aria-pressed
body:
## Summary
The style pills on the wall and the 'try it on' trial chips are single-select button groups that mark the active one only with cyan. MoveDialog, a sibling library surface, does this correctly with aria-pressed.

## Description
LibraryAtelier.tsx:421-429: each style pill is a `<button>` whose only selected signal is `border-cyan-400/40 bg-cyan-400/10 text-cyan-200`. Playground.tsx:258-269: trial chips use the same classes, also with no state attribute. A screen reader hears a row of identical buttons and can't tell which style's sheet is open or which trial subject is loaded. In the same feature, MoveDialog.tsx:333-336 folder buttons carry `type="button" aria-pressed={active}`, and the Discipline `Segmented` directly above the pills (components/ui/Field.tsx:218+) uses real radios. So the pills sit between two correctly built controls with the same look. Neither group sets type="button" either.

## Flow
- Screen reader on the wall: 'Editorial, button', 'Paper cut, button'... no current item
- Fix: add `type="button"` and `aria-pressed={t.id === selected?.id}` on pills; `aria-pressed={subject === t.subject}` on trial chips

## Expected impact
A non-sighted user can tell which style is open and which trial subject is loaded, the same contract MoveDialog already keeps.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - selected state in both chip groups is announced, not just coloured
Before: aria-pressed count: LibraryAtelier.tsx 0, Playground.tsx 0 (MoveDialog.tsx 1)
After: LibraryAtelier.tsx >=1, Playground.tsx >=1
Method: probe - grep count / source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/LibraryAtelier.tsx:421-429 (pill, colour-only state); app/library/Playground.tsx:258-269 (trial chip, colour-only state); app/library/MoveDialog.tsx:333-336 (sibling with aria-pressed); grep -c aria-pressed: LibraryAtelier 0, Playground 0, MoveDialog 1
verify: tests/golden-path/library-atelier-states.probe.spec.ts: stripComments of LibraryAtelier.tsx and Playground.tsx each contain `aria-pressed` (0 on HEAD). npm run typecheck.
